model: OptiPlex Small Form Factor 7010 (2023 model, regulatory model D17S, type D17S003; not the 2012 OptiPlex 7010)
notes: Applies to the 2023 OptiPlex Small Form Factor 7010 (regulatory model D17S, March 2023 manual), not the earlier 2012 OptiPlex 7010 of the same name, which is a different machine. The manual lists a 180 W and a 300 W power supply, so check the label on the unit.

gaps: The copy is on Ingram Micro's content server, not dell.com. Its title page (regulatory model D17S, type D17S003, March 2023, Rev. A00), Dell copyright and PDF author show it is Dell's manual; Dell's own manual page shows no regulatory model, so the copies were not compared.
The manual gives no coin cell type or size, so no CR2032 claim is made.
No chassis (system) fan is described; only the processor fan and heat-sink assembly.
The hard drive's spindle motor and magnets are not named; the entry records the drive options only.
The slim optical drive has no type or rating, so no optical drive part is claimed.
The manual does not say which of the 180 W and 300 W supplies a given unit has.
The 2012 OptiPlex 7010 (MT, DT, SFF and USFF, 3rd generation Intel Core) has its own Dell guidebook; none of its figures are used here.
method: Dell OptiPlex Small Form Factor 7010 Owner's Manual, regulatory model D17S, type D17S003, March 2023, Rev. A00 (inquirecontent2.ingrammicro.com PDF, read as text; the power ratings page (printed p.24) was rendered and checked).

Read: the specifications chapter (audio, storage, power ratings, power supply connectors, GPU and processor tables), the major components list, the speaker, coin-cell, power supply and processor fan and heat-sink sections, and the system board connector list.
Dell's technical guidebook for this model returned HTTP 404; the 2012 OptiPlex 7010 Technical Guidebook (Dell, file dated November 2012) was opened only to tell the two machines apart.

comps.spec: 2023 D17S model, one of two internal PSUs: 180 W (85%, 80 Plus Bronze) or 300 W (92%, 80 Plus Platinum). Input 90-264 VAC, 47-63 Hz, max 3.0 A (180 W) or 4.2 A (300 W). Rated output +12 V on two rails (12 VA, 12 VB); continuous 15 A and 14 A (180 W) or 18 A and 18 A (300 W); standby 1.5 A and 3.3 A.
In the 2023 D17S model: processor fan and heat-sink assembly, four captive screws to the system board, processor-fan cable to the system board
In the 2023 D17S model: hard drive options, SATA 3.0, 2.5-in up to 1 TB or 3.5-in up to 2 TB
In the 2023 D17S model: one internal speaker, average output 2 W and peak 2.5 W, slides out of a chassis slot, cable to the system board
In the 2023 D17S model: coin-cell battery in a system board socket with a release lever

2023 D17S model: PSU cables end in two 4-pin processor connectors and one 8-pin system board connector (both PSU options). The board map also lists SATA power, hard-drive and optical-drive data, speaker, processor-fan, intrusion-switch, power-button and system-power cables.
